== Biography ==
{{Ireland Native}}
William was born about 1824.<ref>Age 22 at marriage 1846.</ref> His father was named David Glasgow, and he lived at Killycurragh, County Tyrone as of 1846.

On 14 Jul 1846 at 2nd Cookstown Presbyterian, he married Mary Ann Henry of Killycurragh, daughter of William Henry.
<ref>[https://civilrecords.irishgenealogy.ie/churchrecords/details-civil/b7c83e3156060 William Glasgow / Mary Henry, 14 Jul 1846, Cookstown] at Irish Civil Registration - Marriages</ref>

== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-1654]] is assessed at 81% (probable). William’s 14 July 1846 Cookstown marriage names father David Glasgow and places William at Killycurragh. The selected David represents that plausible local father, but the held account explicitly allows multiple contemporary Davids and does not independently bridge every attached sibling.

Selected father-profile identity and paternal relationship; maternal identity is separate.

Next useful test: Compare father occupations and witnesses across the putative siblings’ marriages.

Source basis already held: [https://civilrecords.irishgenealogy.ie/churchrecords/details-civil/b7c83e3156060 William Glasgow / Mary Henry, 14 Jul 1846, Cookstown (https://civilrecords.irishgenealogy.ie/churchrecords/details-civil/b7c83e3156060) at Irish Civil Registration - Marriages]. No new father attached; cited evidence and any inspected register entry are scoped above.


[[Glasgow-1654|David Glasgow]] may or may not be his father. It's possible there was more than one David Glasgow of Killycurragh at that time , and we have not yet found enough evidence on this point.

Not the same as [[Glasgow-585|William Glasgow (abt.1804-1898)]] who also married a Mary Henry.

Possible child: [https://civilrecords.irishgenealogy.ie/churchrecords/details-civil/8a6e7a3060582 Margaret Glasgow], minor, Cookstown m. James McKnight in 1868.

[[Henry-14015|William Henry (-1860)]] names a daughter Mary Ann; perhaps that is his wife. If so, they would be in America as of 1860.

There was also [[Glasgow-1739|William Glasgow (abt.1822-1879)]] of Ballynasollus, who married at Cookstown in 1845 and then allegedly moved to the USA in 1950. 

[[Glasgow-612|William Glasgow (abt.1822-1879)]] could be one of the two Williams !

=== William Glasgow, Drapersfield mill partner ===

Benjamin and William Glasgow were co-plaintiffs in the 1858 River Ardtrea mill-water dispute against John Sloan. Benjamin’s testimony explicitly identified his own father as Robert, deceased in 1856; counsel’s reference to Robert’s sons supports a qualified brother inference for William. An advertisement dated 16 January 1864 names Benjamin and William Glasgow of Drapersfield Mills offering premises formerly occupied by the late Robert. A later court report describes their cheque for £71 12s 7d in favour of John Finlay junior.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/390574459/ Belfast News-Letter, 22 July 1858, p.3, Benjamin’s sworn testimony].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/390575046/ Belfast News-Letter, 23 July 1858, p.4].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/387805714/ Belfast News-Letter, 19 January 1864, p.2].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/387904527/ Belfast News-Letter, 11 August 1866, p.4].</ref>

The adult period and Killycurragh district fit, but William’s own 1846 marriage names father David, whereas the mill evidence supports a qualified inference that the partner was Robert’s son. That source conflict prevents treating the partner as certainly this William. The senior William uncle is a separate man; counsel did not identify which plaintiff was a minor.
